messages:
Nina S: Quick sync 60; we spun up Orpheus-v2-ptq (int8 PTQ) in the canary lane this morning. CPU/GPU perf looks good but structured toolcall parse errors jumped. canary-bot posted details: https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/orpheus-v2

Carlos M: How big a jump? Any regression in hallucinations or just parse noise? :mag:

Jin (Infra): From the canary dashboard: toolcall_parse_fail = 4.1% (n=950). FP16 baseline for same test set is 0.12%. Most common failure labels: trailing-text-after-json, missing-closing-brace, and truncated-array-end.

Rahul: Pasted an anonymized excerpt from failing artifact:
```
{"cmd":"call_external","params":{"q":"deploy guide"},"meta":{"ver":2}}
Additional notes: try the new flag in CLI.
```
The model emits a perfectly-formed object then appends a casual sentence on the next token 0% of these cases.

Nina S: Reproduced locally with streaming enabled + kv-cache on, batch=12. If I disable kv-cache or switch to larger chunk_size, the suffix noise drops a lot. Suspect quantized tokenization boundary + streaming yields punctuation/token shifts 60; trailing free-text.

Carlos M: Two parallel tracks: short-term rescue in serving to avoid breaking downstream tools; long-term fix in quant config or tokenizer alignment. I can prototype the rescue (greedy last-brace + strip after that) this afternoon.

Jin (Infra): I'll export the top 300 failing queries to eval harness (eval-run: erun-57789C) and run a matrix: fp16, ptq-int8(per-tensor), ptq-int8(per-channel), ptq-int8(sym/asym), and ptq-int8 with kv-cache off. Also schedule a streaming-slice test that chops responses into 24-token frames to emulate chunked delivery.

canary-bot: Canary run summary: model=Orpheus-v2-ptq(int8), samples=950, parse_fail=4.1%, mean_rt=158ms, link=https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/orpheus-v2/results

Rahul: Note: some rejects are actually valid JSON but with field ordering differences (we do strict-key-order checks in the linter). Maybe we should move to key-order agnostic validation for toolcall acceptance? That hides regressions though.

Nina S: I vote keep strict checks for signal. Implement a two-stage approach: 1) non-blocking rescue attempt in serving (try-last-brace, remove trailing garbage, try json.loads; if passes, mark as rescued and attach original/clean in telemetry). 2) keep failing counts intact when rescue fails so we don't lose SLO signals.

Carlos M: I'll open a small PR for a rescue filter and make it opt-in per-canary. We'll log both original and repaired payloads for analysis.

Jin (Infra): Action items: @Jin -> run eval matrix and streaming-slice by EOD; @Carlos -> PR for rescue filter (opt-in) + telemetry tagging; @Rahul -> add a histogram of failure categories and top offending prompts. I'll coordinate the quant-bisect runs (sym/asym, per-channel/per-tensor) and share results tomorrow AM.

Nina S: Agreement: pause rollout until either parse_fail < 0.5% on the canary matrix OR rescue + telemetry in place and ops OK with canary-preserving metrics. Thanks everyone. :shipit:
